title: Búri: the restoration, the temple, and the world it opens

body:
# Búri: the restoration, the temple, and the world it opens
Every name in this series was once flattened to fit a keyboard. **Búri** is what the evidence put back.

Búri has no adventures, no conflicts, no cult. His entire myth is cosmogonic: he is the first divine being, the point at which the inanimate cosmos becomes personal. Everything that follows in Norse mythology follows from his emergence. In Gylfaginning, Snorri tells how the primeval cow Auðumla licked the salty stones of Niflheimr.  On the first day, hair appeared; on the second, a head; on the third, a whole man.

That is the figure this file is about — and the temple now standing at its restored name.
## At a Glance

- **Restored name:** Búri
- **ASCII form:** buri
- **Meaning:** "In the Prose Edda, Búri is the primeval ancestor born from the salty rime, father of Borr and grandfather of Óðinn."
- **Domain of influence:** First God of the Norse Pantheon, Progenitor of the Æsir
- **Pantheon:** Norse
- **Classification:** Tier 1
- **Original script:** ᛒᚢᚱᛁ
- **Series:** The Restoration Files, No. 52 of 271
## The Name Before the Marks

Strip **Búri** to *buri* and one piece of evidence vanishes:

- **u → ú** — Acute marks stress on u: the stress position the ASCII form cannot show.

A reader who knows the marks hears the name correctly on the first try. A reader who never sees them never gets the chance.
## The Temple That Stands Now

The restored name is not a plaque; it is an address. The temple of **Búri** lives at [/sites/buri/](/sites/buri/), with its mythology in the [lore halls](/sites/buri/lore/), its peer-reviewed record in the [Scholarly Edition](/sites/buri/scholars/), and its place in the pattern atlas on the [patterns floor](/sites/buri/patterns/).

The restoration preserves more than the ASCII form can say — stress, length, or a letter the Latin keyboard lost — which places it in Tier-1: mechanically verifiable, information-rich.

Every flagship temple is hand-built to the same standard: the original script displayed with its provenance, the pronunciation reconstructed phoneme by phoneme, the sources named — because a restoration you cannot audit is just a spelling with confidence.
## The Archetype at Work

A temple is also a reading of what this figure *means* — and meanings have addresses in the modern world. The [pattern atlas](/patterns/) maps **Búri** to the industries its archetype genuinely resonates with, each match argued, weighted, and open to challenge:

- **Ancestry & Heritage Services** — The first god, grandfather of Óðinn; the Norse family tree starts with him.
- **Agriculture, Food & Harvest** — Auðumla, the primeval cow whose licking revealed him — dairy at the dawn of the gods.
- **Mining & Natural Resources** — Licked from the salty rime-stones; the first god is a mineral find.

The mapping is conservative on purpose: only resonances that can be argued aloud. The rest of the atlas follows the same rule, industry by industry.
## In the Sacred Texts

The Norse tradition is not a vibe; it is a library. The [Sacred Texts collection](/texts/) holds [Poetic Edda](/texts/poetic-edda/) and [Prose Edda](/texts/prose-edda/) — the primary sources the temple's scholarship is built on, free to read, cross-linked back to the names they mention. The temple is the argument; the texts are the evidence.
## The File Continues

This is one of 271 Restoration Files — a second dispatch from every flagship temple in the fleet. The temple's [first dispatch](/sites/buri/blog/) tells the founding story of the name; the [blog index](/blog/) holds the whole archive.

Continue the series — previous file: **Bꜣstt** ([read it here](/sites/bastet/blog/restoration/)) · next file: **Qāyīn** ([read it here](/sites/cain/blog/restoration/)).

*The Restoration Files are written from the same canonical record as the temples themselves: the lexicon, the lore catalog, the pattern atlas, and the cited scholarly sources. If a file ever disagrees with its temple, the temple is right — tell us, and the file will be corrected.*
